revision:
ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Retain the full title, controls, Start action, HUD, skier, gates, and trees, but reduce or lift the title card so more of the downhill route is visibly traceable behind it. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Reduce the title panel's height and lift it slightly to reveal more of the slope while preserving the title as the first read. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Choose a base pixel unit and snap all scene geometry, borders, shadows, icons, and decorative marks to multiples of it. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Integrate the title and start prompt into the game world's pixel HUD, add content-driven slope variety such as tracks, moguls, and one iconic hazard, and give the skier a more distinctive animation pose or trail while preserving the strict pixel language. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Retain the full title, controls, Start action, HUD, skier, gates, and trees, but reduce or lift the title card so more of the downhill route is visibly traceable behind it.—while using the clarity action—Reduce the title panel's height and lift it slightly to reveal more of the slope while preserving the title as the first read.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

System consistency versus expression: implement the craft action—Choose a base pixel unit and snap all scene geometry, borders, shadows, icons, and decorative marks to multiples of it.—as the construction grammar, then permit the expressive action—Integrate the title and start prompt into the game world's pixel HUD, add content-driven slope variety such as tracks, moguls, and one iconic hazard, and give the skier a more distinctive animation pose or trail while preserving the strict pixel language.—only as a bounded, content-motivated hero/state exception.

One-round scope versus accumulated requests: prioritize visible requirement ambiguity and the dominant craft defect first; apply secondary typography, spacing, and decorative refinements only when they reuse the same rules and do not trigger a rebuild.
rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
